_README: Rider ids that are variants of one person, and the id they belong to. CONSULTED AT INGEST: without this a re-ingest recreates every absorbed id straight from the scrape files, because the files still carry the old spelling — the same way the Dorsal placeholders came back. Lives outside the DB for that reason, like stage_notes.json and route_type_overrides.json. Produced by audit_rider_duplicates.py + merge_rider_duplicates.py; every entry carries the evidence for the claim, because a merge IS a claim and a wrong one fuses two careers invisibly. The `separated` section is the MIRROR of `aliases`: pairs a human examined and ruled DIFFERENT people. Without it audit_rider_duplicates.py re-proposes them on every run and the next --apply quietly re-merges a decision somebody already made. SPLITS live in rider_splits.json, which is this file's mirror in the other direction: aliases fuse two ids, splits fission one. Four ids were proposed as conflations on 2026-09-12; two survived checking (rider/tom-miller, rider/mark-smith) and are split there, and two did NOT (rider/paul-ellis, rider/mike-johnson) — the reasons are recorded in that file's `rejected` section so nobody re-derives them. rider/paul-c-ellis and rider/mike-t-johnson therefore stay unmerged on the evidence, not on a conflation claim.

rider/aaron-gammell.evidence: Unbound 2010/2011/2012, one rider. Two of his three registrations spell it GAMMEL (2011, 2012) against one Gammell (2010), so the source majority picks the canonical, not string length. A separate Jed Gammell rides Chequamegon with the double L and is a different person.

rider/alejandro-gomez.evidence: Both ids were created for one finisher of The Traka 360 by two sources that spell him differently: PCS's result page and the timer's own ranking. They are the same man because the finish times are identical to the second: 50596s in the 2024 edition, PCS rank 83. PCS's own slug is alejandro-gomez1, and PCS appends that digit only when the bare slug already belongs to someone else. Keeping our locally-minted `alejandro-gomez` would leave a name-shaped id for a rider PCS calls something else, which a later import of that OTHER Alejandro Gomez would land on. The PCS id survives even though it holds no result.

rider/alex-howes-gu.evidence: 'Howes Alex' / 'Alex Howes - GU' differ only by a one extra whole word, they never appear on the same stage, and the birth years the sources imply agree (1988, 1988). That last test is the one carrying the weight: an initial or a generational suffix is exactly what WOULD distinguish a father from a son, so every pair whose implied birth years sat further apart than age-rounding error was left unmerged rather than assumed.

rider/bill-c-stolte.evidence: Chequamegon, one rider entering alternately with and without the middle initial: plain 1999, C in 2000 and 2001, plain again 2002, then plain from 2009 to 2019. The years INTERLEAVE and never collide, which two different Chequamegon regulars sharing a name would not manage for twenty years. Both ids' commonest implied birth year is 1970. NOTE on the evidence NOT used. These eight were held back by a guard that rejected any pair where an id's own rows disagreed about its birth year. That guard turned out to be mostly a proxy for how much age data an id has: across the 63 pairs merged in the same sweep the median id carries ZERO ages and so could not fail it, while these carry a median of three. 75% of the ids here contradict themselves. Athlinks age_at_race is simply noisy at +/-3 to 5 years -- the same failure that records Lachlan Morton as 19 at the 2019 Dirty Kanza when he was 27 -- so it is not evidence either way at that scale. What it can still show is a contradiction too large to be noise, and the four pairs left unmerged are exactly those: rider/tom-miller ages 20 years in 8, rider/mark-smith 7 in 14.
